reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the premises that single-atom Pt resists CO poisoning, is stabilized in a high-entropy alloy, and yields high mass activity and durability in methanol oxidation. However, the hypothesis extends these findings to automotive exhaust oxidation (CO/hydrocarbons) and poisoning by H2O and NO, which are not addressed in the cited methanol oxidation study. The key premise that the catalyst will resist H2O and NO poisoning and enable low-temperature oxidation below 150 °C in exhaust conditions is unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Single-atom Pt sites resist CO poisoning
High-entropy alloy environment stabilizes single-atom Pt sites against degradation
